summary: Wave 3 backend testing: 18/25 passing, 4 skipped (no approved-supplier seed credentials available), 3 REAL failures uncovered. All finance endpoints (summary/dealers/CSV exports with UTF-8 BOM + header row), supplier earnings buyer-forbidden check, paginated search with {results,total,page,pages,limit} and page=999→empty, /api/papers graceful empty list, buyer cannot POST supplier papers, password-reset always-200, admin config write 200/503 (never 500), and the in-memory rate limiter on /api/mps/inquiry (429 with body 'Too many requests…') ALL PASS. Regression: /api/, /listings/search, /printers, /stats/public, /auth/me admin — all 200. 3 NEW failures: (1) GET /api/listings/{uuid} returns 500 (not 404) because `*,suppliers(...,is_suspended)` join blows up — 'column suppliers_1.is_suspended does not exist' — this is the graceful-degrade gap the spec explicitly forbids. (2)+(3) GET /sitemap.xml and GET /robots.txt return the React app's HTML at the public ingress URL because the Kubernetes ingress only routes /api/* to backend:8001 — backend DOES serve them correctly on localhost:8001 (verified: 200 + application/xml with <urlset>, 200 + text/plain with 'Sitemap:' directive) but they're unreachable from the public origin.

critical.issue: Returns 500 instead of 404 for nonexistent UUID. Root cause: select('*,suppliers(business_name,city,is_suspended)') raises postgrest.APIError 'column suppliers_1.is_suspended does not exist' (migration pending). The spec says this endpoint must return 404 or 410, never 500. Fix: wrap the select() in try/except like other endpoints do and fallback to 'suppliers(business_name,city)' when is_suspended is missing.

Both are correctly registered on the bare FastAPI app and return 200 on localhost:8001 (verified: sitemap has <urlset> + /papers + Bangalore; robots has Sitemap directive). But the Kubernetes ingress only routes paths with /api prefix to backend — root-mounted paths fall through to the React frontend, which returns its index.html. As a result, the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/sitemap.xml returns HTML, and robots.txt returns the React frontend's static robots (content signals). Either (a) ingress rule must be added for /sitemap.xml + /robots.txt → backend, or (b) move to /api/sitemap.xml (against spec) or (c) place static files in /app/frontend/public/.

minor.issue: Returns 503 with message hardcoded to a specific .sql filename. Acceptable per spec but couples API error text to migration file naming.
Always returns {ok:true}, even when the email service silently fails — no observability for ops. Consider internal logging counter.

minor.endpoint: (Pre-existing, iteration_6/7) /api/auth/me supplier_status mismatch for rejected applicants; /api/chat missing GOOGLE_API_KEY
minor.issue: Not retested in this iteration — these are documented unresolved issues from prior runs.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): GET /api/listings/{id} must catch the is_suspended-missing exception and fall back to 'suppliers(business_name,city)' — otherwise buyer one-click reorder will 500 across the board until the migration runs.

FIX (HIGH): /sitemap.xml + /robots.txt are unreachable via the public URL because Kubernetes ingress only proxies /api/* to backend:8001. Either (a) update ingress rules to also proxy /sitemap.xml + /robots.txt to backend, or (b) write them as static files into /app/frontend/public/ at build time (preferred for SEO crawlers), or (c) reluctantly move them under /api (against spec).

RUN MIGRATION: /app/backend/supabase_schema_papers.sql — once executed, POST /api/supplier/papers will switch from 503 to 200, GET /api/papers will return real rows, and the is_suspended column referenced by /api/listings/{id} will resolve (also fixing the 500 above as a side-effect).

SEED: Add an approved supplier seed (TEST_SUPPLIER_EMAIL / TEST_SUPPLIER_PASSWORD env vars or seed_supabase.py) so 4 currently-skipped supplier tests (papers create, earnings GET, partial-stock patch) can actually execute end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2705 lines (was 2161 in iteration_7). The wave-3 patch added ~570 lines monolithically. STRONGLY split into routers/admin_finance.py, routers/papers.py, routers/listings_paginated.py, routers/supplier_listings.py, routers/sitemap.py, routers/password_reset.py before another patch lands.

_RATE_BUCKETS is an unbounded in-memory dict — under k8s with > 1 backend pod the rate limit only protects per-pod (caller hitting different pods bypasses the limit). Acceptable for MVP but document; long-term use Redis.
_RATE_BUCKETS also leaks memory forever: keys are 'ip:path' tuples with no eviction. Add a periodic cleanup that drops keys whose latest hit is > window seconds old.

_rate_limit_middleware short-circuits by path string. Because the FastAPI router mounts /api with a prefix, request.url.path will always be '/api/quotation' etc. Confirmed working, but if the prefix ever changes (e.g., /api/v1) the rules dict becomes silently dead. Derive from a constant or attach a marker dep.

GET /api/listings/{id} hits Supabase TWICE conceptually (single select with the suppliers join). When suspended-supplier filter cannot be evaluated (column missing), the endpoint dies entirely. Same vulnerability exists in `/api/papers` but THERE is caught — the inconsistency confirms the missing fallback in `get_listing` is the real bug.

POST /api/supplier/papers raises HTTPException(503, …) `from e` — good — but the entire exception body leaks 'paper_listings table not yet migrated — run supabase_schema_papers.sql' which exposes server-side file naming. Acceptable for an internal alpha; sanitize before public launch.

duplicate_listing/duplicate_printer blindly copy ALL columns from the source row (except id/created_at/updated_at). If the source has 'sku' or 'slug' columns with unique constraints, the insert will 409. Today neither table has such constraints, but worth defending.

sitemap_xml hardcodes base='https://www.tonerscart.com' — fine for production but means the dev preview environment will publish wrong canonical URLs if any crawler ever fetches it via the dev URL. Pull from env (SITEMAP_BASE_URL) with that as the default.

/api/listings/search/paginated reuses search_listings(limit=2000) and slices in memory — for total >2000 the 'total' figure is capped at 2000 and pages are wrong. Switch to a count+range query in Supabase before listing volume crosses ~1000 active rows.

PUT /api/supplier/listings/{id} silently accepts payload with no valid fields (negative stock, zero price) and returns {ok:true, updated:[]} — caller cannot tell whether the row exists or if the payload was rejected. Return 400 on empty/invalid patch.

GET /api/admin/finance/summary fetches up to 10000 orders with a 'listings' join every call. With production traffic this will be slow and bandwidth-heavy. Cache for ~5 min or pre-aggregate in Supabase via a materialised view.

compress_image swallows all Pillow exceptions and silently returns the original bytes — if a malicious payload is crafted, we may end up storing the unmodified raw blob instead of the resized JPEG. Log the failure at WARNING (not DEBUG) and consider rejecting unrecognised formats outright.

The 4 supplier-skipped tests will only execute once an approved supplier seed exists. Regression: tests/test_admin_v2.py (22 admin v2 tests) and tests/test_polish_patch.py (15 polish-patch tests) were not re-run this iteration — they were green in iteration_6/7 and the wave-3 patch is additive (no modifications to admin_v2 / polish endpoints visible in the diff). If main agent fixes the get_listing 500, re-run only this file plus test_admin_v2 to confirm no regression in suspended-supplier filter behavior.
rca of the issue: (1) GET /api/listings/{id} 500: server.py:2596 does `select('*,suppliers(business_name,city,is_suspended)')`; the is_suspended column on suppliers is part of the deferred admin_v2 migration (supabase_schema_admin_v2.sql) which has NOT been run. PostgREST returns 'column suppliers_1.is_suspended does not exist' and FastAPI re-raises as 500. Spec explicitly says 'GET /api/listings/{nonexistent_uuid} → 404 (not 500)'. Mitigation: wrap in try/except like /api/papers does (see server.py:2444-2474 for the pattern) and fallback to the join without is_suspended. (2)+(3) sitemap.xml / robots.txt: backend correctly mounts them on the bare `app` (not under /api). Verified via curl http://localhost:8001/sitemap.xml → 200 + application/xml + <urlset>. The kubernetes ingress, however, only routes /api/* to backend port 8001; all other paths go to the React frontend on port 3000. The React app's index.html catch-all serves /sitemap.xml, returning HTML. Mitigation: either add an ingress rule for those two exact paths, or generate them at build time into /app/frontend/public/ (CRA serves /app/frontend/public/* as static).
